### **1.3 User Requirements** {#1.3-user-requirements}

#### **1.3.1 Actors**

| \# | Actor | Description |
| :---: | :---: | ----- |
| 1 | Administrator | Responsible for configuring and maintaining the system. The Administrator manages user accounts, roles and permissions, service catalogs, inventory categories, pricing policies, suppliers, and system configuration data. The Administrator can also monitor operational reports and system-wide information.  |
| 2 | Manager | Responsible for managing the complete order lifecycle and operational activities. The Manager creates and updates orders, schedules surveys, allocates staff, manages inventory allocation, prepares quotations, processes payments, coordinates deployments, verifies operational results, and monitors dashboards and reports.  |
| 3 |  Leader Staff  | Responsible for executing and supervising on-site operations. The Leader Staff performs surveys, supervises equipment loading and transportation, updates installation progress, records change requests, handles customer payments, manages equipment retrieval and inventory returns, submits operational reports, and confirms staff attendance.  |
| 4 | Technical Staff  | Responsible for performing assigned operational tasks. The Technical Staff views assigned tasks and order details, prepares equipment, confirms task completion, and records attendance for payroll calculation.  |
| 5 | VNPay Payment Gateway  | An external payment system that supports QR code generation and online payment processing. It communicates with the system to facilitate customer payment transactions and provide payment status information.  |

Table I \- 1.3.1: Actors

#### **1.3.2 Use Cases**

##### **1.3.2.1. Use Cases Description**

| ID | Use Case | Role | Use Case Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| UC-ID-01 | Login | All | Allows users to log in using their credentials. |
| UC-ID-02 | Logout | All | Allows users to securely end their current session. |
| UC-ID-03 | Forgot Password | All | Allows users to recover access when they forget their password. |
| UC-ID-04 | Change Password | All | Allows authenticated users to change their current password. |
| UC-ID-05 | View Profile | All | Allows users to view their personal profile. |
| UC-ID-06 | Receive Notifications | All | Allows users to receive system, operational, and task-related notifications based on their roles and assigned responsibilities.  |
| UC-ID-07 | View User List | Admin | Allows Admin to view internal user accounts. |
| UC-ID-08 | Create User Information | Admin | Allows Admin to create a new internal user account. |
| UC-ID-09 | Update User Information | Admin | Allows Admin to update an existing user account and profile information.  |
| UC-ID-10 | Deactivate User | Admin | Allows Admin to deactivate a user account. |
| UC-ID-11 | Reset User Password | Admin | Allows Admin to reset a user’s password. |
| UC-ID-12 | Assign Role to User | Admin | Allows Admin to assign or change a user’s role. |
| UC-ID-13 | View Equipment Catalog | Admin | Allows Admin to view equipment catalog information. |
| UC-ID-14 | Create Equipment | Admin | Allows Admin to create a new equipment item. |
| UC-ID-15 | Update Equipment | Admin | Allows Admin to update equipment information. |
| UC-ID-16 | Deactivate Equipment | Admin | Allows Admin to deactivate an equipment item while keeping historical records. |
| UC-ID-17 | View Supplier List | Manager | Allows Manager to view supplier information. |
| UC-ID-18 | Create Supplier | Manager | Allows Manager to create a new supplier record. |
| UC-ID-19 | Update Supplier | Manager | Allows Manager to update supplier information. |
| UC-ID-20 | Deactivate Supplier | Manager | Allows Manager to deactivate a supplier for future transactions. |
| UC-ID-21 | View Warehouse Information | Admin | Allows Admin to view warehouse information. |
| UC-ID-22 | View Policy List | Admin | Allows Admin to view configured business policies in the system.  |
| UC-ID-23 | Create Policy | Admin | Allows Admin to create a new business policy for deposit, cancellation, compensation, additional fees, or wage rules.  |
| UC-ID-24 | Update Policy | Admin | Allows Admin to update an existing business policy when business rules change.  |
| UC-ID-25 | Deactivate Policy | Admin | Allows Admin to deactivate a business policy that is no longer applied while keeping historical records.  |
| UC-ID-26 | View Administrative Dashboard | Admin | Allows Admin to view summarized reports and audit-oriented operational data. |
| UC-ID-27 | View Operational Dashboard | Manager | Allows Manager to view order status, task progress, payment status, inventory status, and operational issues. |
| UC-ID-28 | View Revenue Reports | Admin | Allows Admin to view revenue reports for overall business monitoring and audit. |
| UC-ID-29 | View Order Statistics | Admin | Allows Admin to view summarized order statistics for audit and management purposes. |
| UC-ID-30 | View Inventory Reports & Statistics  | Admin | Allows Admin to view summarized inventory statistics, equipment status, inventory return reports, damage/loss summaries, maintenance-related inventory status, and related audit data.  |
| UC-ID-31 | View Customer Information | Manager | Allows Manager to view customer information. |
| UC-ID-32 | Register Customer | Manager | Allows Manager to register a new customer. |
| UC-ID-33 | Update Customer | Manager | Allows Manager to update customer information. |
| UC-ID-34 | Create Quotation | Manager | Allows Manager to create a quotation for a customer order. |
| UC-ID-35 | View Quotation | Manager  | Allows Manager to view quotation details before updating, confirming, or sending quotation information to the customer outside the system.  |
| UC-ID-36 | Update Quotation | Manager | Allows Manager to update quotation details after changes. |
| UC-ID-37 | Delete Quotation | Manager  | Allows Manager to delete or remove a draft quotation that has not been confirmed or linked to an active confirmed order.  |
| UC-ID-38 | Confirm Quotation | Manager | Allows Manager to confirm the quotation agreed with the customer. |
| UC-ID-39 | View Order List | Manager | Allows Manager to view the list of orders for operational processing. |
| UC-ID-40 | View Order Details | Manager | Allows Manager to view detailed order information, including customer, quotation, payment, assignment, inventory, and operation data. |
| UC-ID-41 | Track Order Status | Manager | Allows Manager to monitor the current status and progress of an order throughout its lifecycle. |
| UC-ID-42 | Create Order | Manager | Allows Manager to create a new customer order. |
| UC-ID-43 | Update Order | Manager | Allows Manager to update order information. |
| UC-ID-44 | Confirm Order | Manager | Allows Manager to confirm an order after quotation agreement and valid deposit confirmation. After confirmation, the system reserves required internal inventory by event date.  |
| UC-ID-45 | Change Event Date | Manager  | Allows Manager to change the event date according to date-change policy. The system rechecks inventory for the new date, releases the previous reservation, and reserves inventory for the new event date if available.  |
| UC-ID-46 | Cancel Order | Manager | Allows Manager to cancel an order, apply refund policy, and automatically release reserved inventory if applicable.  |
| UC-ID-47 | Confirm Order Closure | Manager | Allows Manager to review all final order data, including deposit payment, final payment, payment evidence, handover report, damage/loss records if any, settlement, inventory return, supplier return/debt, and staff work/wage data before confirming order closure. After Manager confirms that all required data are valid, the system updates the order status to Completed.  |
| UC-ID-48 | Create Schedule Plan  | Manager | Allows Manager to create a schedule plan for survey, preparation, transportation, execution, collection, and return activities.  |
| UC-ID-49 | Edit Schedule Plan | Manager | Allows Manager to edit an existing schedule plan when timing, staff assignment, transportation, or operation details change.  |
| UC-ID-50 | View Schedule Plan List  | Manager | Allows Manager to view schedule plans for operational coordination and follow-up.  |
| UC-ID-51 | Delete Schedule Plan | Manager  | Allows Manager to delete a draft or unused schedule plan if it has not affected confirmed assignments or active tasks.  |
| UC-ID-52 | Create Work Task for Staff | Manager  | Allows Manager to create work tasks for staff.  |
| UC-ID-53 | Assign Work Task for Staff | Manager | Allows Manager to assign work tasks to staff.  |
| UC-ID-54 | Edit Work Task for Staff | Manager | Allows Manager to edit staff work task information when schedule, staff, location, or execution requirements change.  |
| UC-ID-55 | Delete Work Task for Staff  | Manager | Allows Manager to delete a draft or incorrect staff task before it is executed.  |
| UC-ID-56 | Monitor Survey Progress | Manager | Allows Manager to track survey progress. |
| UC-ID-57 | View Survey Report | Manager | Allows Manager to review submitted survey reports. |
| UC-ID-58 | Check Inventory Availability  | Manager | Allows Manager to check or recheck internal inventory availability by event date before survey, after survey, or when order requirements change. The result supports quotation, supplier planning, and order confirmation decisions.  |
| UC-ID-59 | Generate Pick List | Manager | Allows Manager to generate a pick list for preparation, check-out, delivery, installation, collection, and return tasks. |
| UC-ID-60 | Confirm Inventory Check-out | Manager  | Allows Manager to view and confirm inventory check-out information submitted by Leader Staff, including checked-out items, quantities, notes, and evidence if required.  |
| UC-ID-61 | Confirm Inventory Return Report  | Manager | Allows Manager to view, verify, and confirm inventory return records after comparing check-out, collection, damage/loss, and return data.  |
| UC-ID-62 | Create Supplier Rental/Purchase Order  | Manager  | Allows Manager to create a supplier rental or purchase order when internal inventory is insufficient or additional materials/equipment are required. Manager may save the order as draft or confirm it after supplier details, items, quantity, cost, and expected delivery information have been agreed with the Supplier outside the system.  |
| UC-ID-63 | View Supplier Rental/Purchase Order List  | Manager  | Allows Manager to view the list of supplier rental and purchase orders, including supplier, order reference, items, quantity, cost, payment status, and transaction status.  |
| UC-ID-64 | Update Supplier Rental/Purchase Order  | Manager  | Allows Manager to update supplier rental or purchase order information, such as supplier, item list, quantity, cost, expected delivery date, notes, and payment-related information before the supplier rental/purchase order is confirmed, received, or linked to supplier debt/payment records.  |
| UC-ID-65 | Delete Supplier Rental/Purchase Order  | Manager  | Allows Manager to delete a draft or incorrect supplier rental/purchase order only if it has not been confirmed, received, paid, or linked to supplier debt records.  |
| UC-ID-66 | Confirm Supplier Equipment Rental / Purchase Report | Manager | Allows Manager to view, verify and confirm supplier equipment rental or purchase report information. |
| UC-ID-67 | Confirm Supplier Equipment Receipt Report  | Manager | Allows Manager to view, verify and confirm supplier equipment receipt information submitted by Leader Staff, including received items, quantity, condition, notes, and evidence if required.  |
| UC-ID-68 | Confirm Supplier Equipment Return Report (with Equipment Rental)  | Manager  | Allows Manager to view, verify, and confirm returned supplier equipment quantity, condition, and compensation information if applicable.  |
| UC-ID-69 | Monitor Supplier Debt | Manager | Allows Manager to track supplier costs and outstanding payments. |
| UC-ID-70 | Record Supplier Payment | Manager | Allows Manager to record payment status for supplier transactions. |
| UC-ID-71 | Confirm Staff Work and Wage  | Manager | Allows Manager to verify valid working sessions of Leader Staff and Technical Staff based on assignments, attendance, completed tasks, wage rules, wage rates, and deductions before wage reporting.  |
| UC-ID-72 | Monitor Field Operation Progress | Manager | Allows Manager to monitor warehouse preparation, transportation, setup/construction, collection, return progress, and arising field issues. |
| UC-ID-73 | Approve Change Request | Manager | Allows Manager to approve or reject add/remove/replace equipment requests submitted by Leader Staff during field execution. |
| UC-ID-74 | Confirm Handover Report | Manager | Allows Manager to verify and confirm handover information and evidence submitted by Leader Staff. |
| UC-ID-75 | Confirm Damage/Loss Report | Manager  | Allows Manager to verify and confirm damage/loss reports. |
| UC-ID-76 | Create Deposit Payment Request | Manager | Allows Manager to create a deposit payment request after the Customer has agreed with the quotation outside the system. The request includes deposit amount, payment method options, due date if applicable, and payment instructions for the Customer.   |
| UC-ID-77 | Generate QR Payment  | Manager , VNPay (secondary actor) | Allows Manager to generate a QR payment code through VNPay Gateway when the Customer chooses QR payment for deposit or final payment. After the Customer completes the payment successfully, the system may automatically update the payment transaction status based on the response from VNPay Gateway.  |
| UC-ID-78 | Confirm Deposit  | Manager | Allows Manager to confirm the Customer’s deposit payment after the deposit payment request has been created. If the Customer pays through VNPay QR, the system may automatically update the payment status after successful transaction confirmation. If the Customer pays by cash, Manager must verify uploaded payment evidence before confirming the deposit payment.  |
| UC-ID-79 | Confirm Settlement | Manager  | Allows Manager to review and confirm the final settlement amount after the event. The settlement includes original order value, change request adjustments, additional fees, customer compensation for damaged or lost equipment if any, deposit paid, previous payments, and the remaining amount to be collected.  |
| UC-ID-80 | Confirm Final Payment  | Manager  | Allows Manager to confirm the Customer’s final payment after settlement has been confirmed. If the final payment is made through VNPay QR, the system may automatically update the payment status after successful transaction confirmation. If the payment is made by cash or manual bank transfer, Manager must verify uploaded payment evidence before confirming the final payment.  |
| UC-ID-81 | View Assigned Tasks | Leader Staff, Technical Staff | Allows staff to view assigned tasks. |
| UC-ID-82 | View Task Details | Leader Staff, Technical Staff | Allows staff to view task details, assigned order summary, location, schedule, checklist, and required execution notes.  |
| UC-ID-83 | View Pick List | Leader Staff, Technical Staff | Allows staff to view equipment pick lists for assigned preparation, delivery, setup, collection, or return tasks.  |
| UC-ID-84 | Record Survey Report | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record site survey information, upload images, and submit the survey report to Manager |
| UC-ID-85 | Record Warehouse Check-out Report | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record actual warehouse check-out information, including checked-out items, quantities, notes, and evidence if required.  |
| UC-ID-86 | Record Supplier Equipment Receipt Report  | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record received supplier equipment. |
| UC-ID-87 | Record Supplier Equipment Return Report (with Equipment Rental)  | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record returned supplier equipment and its condition for Manager review.  |
| UC-ID-88 | Update Field Progress | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to update transportation, installation, collection, warehouse return progress, and mark field work status based on evidence and actual supervision.  |
| UC-ID-89 | Upload Handover Evidence  | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to upload handover evidence, such as completed setup photos, handover images, or related proof  |
| UC-ID-90 | Record Change Request | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record customer change requests at the event site and submit them for Manager approval.  |
| UC-ID-91 | Record Damage/Loss Report | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record damaged or lost equipment with evidence. |
| UC-ID-92 | Record Collected Equipment | Leader Staff  | Allows Leader Staff to record equipment collected after the event before warehouse return. |
| UC-ID-93 | Record Inventory Return Report | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to submit inventory return information for Manager verification. |
| UC-ID-94 | Check-in Attendance | Leader Staff, Technical Staff | Allows staff to check-in attendance for assigned work sessions. |
| UC-ID-95 | Confirm Technical Staff Attendance & Work Completion | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to confirm Technical Staff’s attendance and task completion for assigned work sessions based on actual supervision, assigned tasks, attendance records, completion status, and supporting notes or evidence if required. The confirmed result is used as supporting data for Manager to verify staff work and wage.  |
| UC-ID-96 | Upload Customer Payment Evidence | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to upload Customer payment evidence at the event site, such as cash receipt images or bank transfer screenshots, when the Customer makes an on-site payment. The uploaded evidence is submitted to Manager for payment verification and confirmation.  |
| UC-ID-97 | Record Settlement  | Leader Staff | Allows Leader Staff to record on-site settlement information after the event, including extra charges, damage/loss compensation, remaining payment information, payment notes, and uploaded payment evidence if the Customer pays on site. The settlement information is submitted to Manager for review, settlement confirmation, and final payment confirmation.  |

#### **1.4.3 Non-UI Functions**

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Authentication Management | User Authentication | Verify login credentials, account status, and create a valid user session. |
| 2 | Authentication Management | Password Management | Hash passwords, validate password rules, and process password reset requests. |
| 3 | Authorization Management | Role-Based Access Control | Control access to screens, actions, and APIs based on user roles and permissions. |
| 4 | User & Permission Management | User Account Validation | Validate user information, role, account status, and uniqueness when creating or updating accounts. |
| 5 | Audit Management | Audit Log Recording | Record important system actions such as login, user updates, approvals, payments, and policy changes. |
| 6 | Notification Management | Notification Processing | Generate and send notifications for task assignments, approvals, payments, surveys, and field progress. |
| 7 | Master Data Management | Master Data Validation | Validate equipment, service, package, supplier, warehouse, pricing, and policy data before use. |
| 8 | Policy Configuration | Business Policy Evaluation | Apply deposit, cancellation, refund, compensation, additional fee, and staff wage policies. |
| 9 | Quotation Management | Quotation Calculation | Calculate quotation value based on selected services, equipment, packages, quantities, discounts, and extra fees. |
| 10 | Order Lifecycle Management | Order Workflow Processing | Control order status transitions from creation, quotation, deposit, execution, settlement, and completion. |
| 11 | Inventory Management | Date-based Inventory Checking | Check equipment availability by event date and prevent inventory double-booking. |
| 12 | Inventory Management | Inventory Reservation Processing | Reserve equipment for confirmed orders and release reservations when orders are changed or cancelled. |
| 13 | Staff Assignment Management | Staff Assignment Validation | Check staff availability, role suitability, and task schedule before assigning staff. |
| 14 | Field Operation Management | Field Progress Processing | Store task progress, completion status, notes, issues, and evidence submitted by field staff. |
| 15 | Change Request Management | Change Request Processing | Process submission, approval, rejection, and tracking of field change requests. |
| 16 | Payment & Settlement Management | Payment Processing | Generate QR payment, verify payment evidence or gateway response, and update payment status. |
| 17 | Attendance & Wage Management | Attendance and Wage Calculation | Validate attendance records and calculate staff wages based on confirmed tasks and wage rules. |
| 18 | Reporting Management | Report Aggregation | Aggregate data for revenue, orders, inventory, supplier debt, staff wage, and operational reports. |

Table IV \-1.4.3:Non- UI Functions

### **1.5 Entity Relationship Diagram** {#1.5-entity-relationship-diagram}

**![][image15]**

Figure XIV \- 1.5. Entity Relationship Diagram ([Link](https://online.visual-paradigm.com/share.jsp?id=333833313535312d3138))

| \# | Entity | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Internal User | Internal personnel who can log in to the system, including Admin, Manager, Leader Staff, and Technical Staff.  |
| 2 | Customer | Customer who books wedding/event services. The Customer is the source of orders but does not log in to or directly use the system.  |
| 3 | Supplier | External partner that supplies, rents, or sells equipment/materials for an order when internal inventory is insufficient or additional items are needed.  |
| 4 | Catalog Item | Catalog of services, equipment, materials, consumables, or packages used in quotations, orders, inventory, or supplier transactions.  |
| 5 | Business Policy | Set of configurable business policies, including deposit, refund, cancellation, date change, additional fee, discount, and compensation policies.  |
| 6 | Order | Core entity of the system, representing a service request/contract from a Customer, from initial request to completion or cancellation.  |
| 7 | Quotation | Quotation version created by the Manager for an Order before the Customer agrees and the Order is confirmed.  |
| 8 | Payment | Financial transaction between the Customer and the business, including deposit, final payment, on-site payment, or customer refund.  |
| 9 | Settlement | Final financial reconciliation of an Order, summarizing order value, additional charges, compensation, received payments, and remaining amount.  |
| 10 | Change Request | On-site change request from the Customer, such as adding, removing, or replacing items in an Order.  |
| 11 | Work Task | Specific operational tasks required to complete an Order, such as survey, preparation, checkout, transportation, installation, collection, or warehouse return.  |
| 12 | Assignment | Allocation of a Work Task to a specific Internal User, identifying which staff member is assigned to which task.  |
| 13 | Warehouse | Main physical warehouse of the business used to store equipment/materials and manage checkout, return, and inventory adjustment activities.  |
| 14 | Inventory | Actual stock data of each Catalog Item in the Warehouse, including available, reserved, checked-out, in-use, maintenance, damaged, and lost quantities.  |
| 15 | Warehouse History | Warehouse transaction history recording checkout, return, receiving, returning, inventory adjustment, or item condition updates.  |
| 16 | Supplier Transaction | Rental or purchase transaction with a Supplier for a specific Order.  |
| 17 | Handover Record | Acceptance and handover record after installation, recording handover status, Customer agreement, and related evidence. |
| 18 | Damage/Loss Report | Report recording damaged or lost equipment/materials during collection, inspection, or warehouse return.  |
| 19 | Supplier Debt  | Debt amount owed to a Supplier from Supplier Transactions, including rental/purchase costs and compensation if any.  |
| 20 | Attendance | Attendance data of Leader Staff or Technical Staff based on Assignment, working date, and working session.  |
| 21 | Wage Summary | Wage summary of each staff member for a wage period, usually monthly, based on confirmed Attendance records.  |
| 22 | Evidence  | Evidence uploaded to the system, including photos, receipts, payment proofs, handover images, survey photos, or damage/loss images.  |
| 23 | Notification | Internal notification sent by the system to an Internal User, such as task assignment, confirmation request, pending payment approval, or field report alert.  |

Table V \- 1.5. Entities Description

## **2\. Use Case Specifications** {#2.-use-case-specifications}

### **2.1. Authentication**

#### **2.1.1. Login**

##### **UC-ID-01: Login**

| Primary Actors | Admin, Manager, Leader Staff, Technical Staff |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Secondary Actors** | None |
| **Description** | As an internal user, I want to log in using my credentials. |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The user account has been created and authorized. 2\. The user account is active and not locked. 3\. The user accesses the correct platform for their role. |
| **Postconditions** | 1\. The user logs into the system successfully. 2\. The system creates a valid user session/token. 3\. The system records successful login activity. 4\. The user is redirected to the appropriate homepage or previous requested page. |
| **Normal Sequences/ Flow** | 1\. User opens the Web or Mobile application. 2\. System displays the Login screen. 3\. User enters login details, including username and password. 4\. User clicks the Login button. 5\. System validates the login details according to authentication rules. 6\. System allows the user to access the system. 7\. System records the successful login activity in the Activity Log. 8\. System redirects the user to the role-based homepage or the previous requested page. |
| **Alternative Sequences/ Flow** | A1: Required login information is missing 1\. At step 3, the user leaves the username and/or password field blank. 2\. The client displays a validation message. 3\. The user enters the missing information. 4\. The process returns to step 3 of the normal flow. |
| **Exception Flows** | E1: System cannot authenticate the user 1\. At step 5, the system cannot authenticate the user. 2\. The system returns an authentication error response in one of the following cases: username or password is incorrect, user account is inactive or deactivated, user account is locked, or user role does not have permission to access the selected platform. 3\. The client displays the corresponding error message. 4\. The user may correct login information or contact Admin if needed. 5\. The use case ends.   E2: Failed login attempts exceed limit 1\. At step 5, the user enters incorrect login details repeatedly. 2\. The system detects that failed login attempts reach the configured limit. 3\. The system temporarily locks the account. 4\. The system returns a lock warning response. 5\. The client displays the warning message. 6\. The use case ends. |
| **Business Rules** | BR-LG01: Users must log in using username and password only. BR-LG02: The system must verify account status before granting access. BR-LG03: Role and platform permission must be checked after authentication. BR-LG04: Repeated failed login attempts may temporarily lock the account. BR-LG05: Successful login activity must be recorded for audit purposes. |
| **Messages** | MSG-LG01: Username or password is incorrect. MSG-LG02: This account is inactive or deactivated. MSG-LG03: This account is temporarily locked. Please try again later. MSG-LG04: Your role is not allowed to access this platform. MSG-LG05: Too many failed login attempts. Your account has been temporarily locked. MSG-LG06: Login successful. |

 Table VI \- 2.1.1.Login

#### **2.1.2. Logout**

##### **UC-ID-02: Logout**

| Primary Actors | Admin, Manager, Leader Staff, Technical Staff |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Secondary Actors** | None |
| **Description** | As an internal user, I want to securely end my current session. |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The user has logged into the system. 2\. A valid user session or token exists. |
| **Postconditions** | 1\. The current user session is terminated. 2\. Authentication tokens or session data are invalidated. 3\. The logout activity is recorded. 4\. The user is redirected to the Login screen. |
| **Normal Sequences/ Flow** | 1\. User selects the Logout option. 2\. System receives the logout request. 3\. System invalidates the current session/token. 4\. System records the logout activity. 5\. System redirects the user to the Login screen. |
| **Alternative Sequences/ Flow** | A1: Actor cancels the action 1\. The system does not save changes. 2\. The process returns to the previous screen. |
| **Exception Flows** | E1: Required information is missing or invalid 1\. The system detects missing required fields, invalid data, unavailable status, invalid evidence, or unauthorized access. 2\. The client displays the corresponding error message (MSG-UC02-01). 3\. Admin, Manager, Leader Staff, Technical Staff corrects the information if possible. 4\. The process returns to the related step of the normal flow.   E2: System cannot complete the request 1\. The system cannot complete the request due to data conflict, system error, unavailable external service, or invalid workflow status. 2\. The client displays the error message (MSG-UC02-02). 3\. Admin, Manager, Leader Staff, Technical Staff retries later or contacts the responsible user if needed. 4\. The use case ends. |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02-01: Only authorized actor(s) can perform this use case. BR-02-02: Required information must be validated before the system saves, submits, confirms, or displays the result. BR-02-03: The use case must follow role-based access control and current workflow status. BR-02-04: Successful business activities must be recorded in the Activity Log for audit purposes. BR-02-05: Active sessions must be protected from unauthorized access. BR-02-06: Password recovery must require identity verification before access is restored. |
| **Messages** | MSG-UC02-01: Required information is missing or invalid. MSG-UC02-02: System cannot complete the request at this time. MSG-UC02-03: You do not have permission to perform this action. MSG-UC02-04: Logout completed successfully. |

 Table VII \- 2.1.2.Logout

### **3.1  Authentication Feature** {#3.1-authentication-feature}

#### **3.1.1 Authentication**

##### **3.1.1.1 User Login Screen**

* **Mockup Layout:**

  **![][image16]**


Figure XV \- 3.1.1.1. User Login Screen

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Email/Username | Text Box | Input area for the user's unique identity credentials (either their system email or alpha-numeric username). |
| 2 | Password | Password Box | Input area for the user's private security key. Characters are automatically masked with \* indicators. |
| 3 | Remember Me | Checkbox | Optional flag to persist an active web or app session locally on the current user workstation. |
| 4 | Forgot Password | Hyperlink | Navigation anchor routing users to the automated recovery request interface if they lose account access. |
| 5 | Login Button | Button | Interactive action element that compiles and transmits credential payloads to the authentication engine. |

  **![][image17]**

* **Component Specification Table:**

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Email | Text Box | Input field for entering the verified email address bound to the user's internal account ledger. |

| 3 | Back to Login | Hyperlink | Simple cancellation link that discards inputs and reverts the user to the basic Login page view. |

**![][image18]**

Figure XVII \- 3.1.1.3. Reset Password Screen

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | New Password | Password Box | Input field where users type their brand-new, updated authentication password string. |

##### **3.1.2.1 Profile**

* **Mockup Layout:**

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |

| 5 | Change Password Button | Button | Interactive action element that redirects the user to the secure password modification interface. |
| 6 | Date Joined | Label | Non-interactive metadata text showing the exact registration date of the account in the system. |
| 7 | Last Login | Label | Non-interactive metadata text displaying the timestamp of the user's most recent successful authentication. |

##### **![][image20]**

Figure XIX \- 3.1.2.2. Change Password Screen

* **Component Specification Table:**

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Close Button (X) | Icon Button | Functional icon to close the change password popup modal and return to the main Profile screen without saving changes. |

| 3 | New Password | Password Box | Input area where the user enters their desired new secure password. Characters are automatically masked. |
| 4 | Confirm New Password | Password Box | Input area to re-enter the new password, ensuring consistency and preventing typographical errors. Characters are automatically masked. |
| 5 | Cancel Button | Button | Interactive element that dismisses the popup modal, discarding any inputted text and retaining the existing password. |
| 6 | Update Password Button | Button | Interactive action element that triggers validation checks on credential rules and updates the security configuration in the authentication system. |

#### **3.2.1 User List**

* **Mockup Layout:**

**![][image21]**

Figure XX \- 3.2.1.User List

* **Brief Description:** This screen allows administrators or authorized personnel to view, search, filter, and manage all user accounts within the enterprise system. It displays key information such as name, email, system role, account status, and last login activity in a structured tabular format.  
* **Component Specification Table:**

| No. | Component Name | Type | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Refresh Button | Button (Icon) | Triggers a data reload to fetch the latest user records from the database without refreshing the entire web page. |
| 2 | Create User Button | Button | Interactive action element that opens the creation form or modal to register a new user into the system. |
| 3 | Search Input Field | Text Box | Input area that allows real-time or keyword-based filtering of the user list by name or email address. |
| 4 | Role Filter | Dropdown | Filter component that restricts the displayed list based on specific user roles (e.g., Admin, Manager, User). Default value is "All Roles". |
| 5 | Status Filter | Dropdown | Filter component that restricts the user list based on account activity state (e.g., Active, Inactive). Default value is "All Statuses". |
| 6 | User Data Table | Table | Structured grid that lists user details categorized under columns: Full Name (with avatar/initials), Email, Role, Status, Last Login, and Actions. |
| 7 | Pagination Controls | Pagination | Navigation controls (Previous, Page numbers 1, 2, 3..., Next) that allow the administrator to browse through multi-page data entries. |

## **4\. Non-Functional Requirements** {#4.-non-functional-requirements}

### **4.1 External Interfaces** {#4.1-external-interfaces}

* **User Interfaces:**  
  * Web Administration Dashboard: The system provides a centralized web-based interface designed exclusively for the Admin and Manager roles. This platform is responsible for managing system configurations, master data initialization, role-based permission matrices, end-to-end order lifecycles, and operational or financial report approvals.  
  * Mobile Application: A dedicated cross-platform mobile application optimized specifically for field personnel, including Leader Staff and Technical Staff. The app supports immediate field tasks such as digital site surveys, image uploads, warehouse check-out/in checklist interactions, real-time damage logging, and displaying dynamic on-screen VietQR settlement codes.  
  * UI Layout Standards: Both Web (React) and Mobile (Flutter) interfaces must adhere strictly to unified branding guidelines, ensuring clean screen layouts, logical item positioning, and balanced color palettes across both platforms to guarantee high structural consistency.  
* **Hardware Interfaces:**  
  * The mobile application must operate seamlessly on the personal smartphone devices of the technical field staff.  
  * The field mobile devices must have a fully functioning built-in camera that satisfies baseline resolution requirements to record clear visual evidence during site surveys and document damaged or lost equipment.  
* **Software Interfaces:**  
  * Database Management Systems: The application interfaces with a structured MySQL relational database to process transactional data grids (such as catalog data, pricing rules, and orders) and utilizes a Firebase environment for live document state synchronization.  
  * Notification Push Services: The backend integrates directly with Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to instantly trigger automated push alerts, dispatch notifications, and schedule updates directly to the mobile devices of assigned field staff.  
  * Deployment Server Infrastructure: The entire application backend API and core database engines are hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), utilizing Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances for compute nodes and Relational Database Service (RDS) for managed database storage.  
* **Communication Interfaces:**  
  * All field operations and mobile app synchronization behaviors require a stable Internet connection (via 4G/5G cellular networks or Wi-Fi networks) to ensure immediate data transmission to the central database server.  
  * Payment Gateway Integration: The platform implements standard secure API hooks connecting to the VNPay gateway to handle automated deposit recording and digital transfer verifications.  
  * Dynamic QR Generation: The app leverages dynamic VietQR API integrations to construct unique, order-specific settlement codes containing exact remaining balance parameters directly on the technician's mobile screen.

### **4.2 Quality Attributes** {#4.2-quality-attributes}

#### **4.2.1 Usability:** 

* Localized Workflow Adaptability: The entire system interface must be built in the Vietnamese language and customized precisely to domestic wedding service conventions, completely eliminating the steep learning curves and generic workflow friction found in traditional Western platforms like Current RMS.  
* Simplified Field Task Operation: On-site execution milestones are broken down into intuitive mobile checklist routines and point-and-click actions, ensuring that general technical workers can operate the app successfully with minimal technical training or onboarding.

#### **4.2.2 Performance:**

* Real-time Collision Prevention: The automated Date-based Inventory Engine must track item availability instantaneously upon order confirmations, maintaining a strict 0% overbooking or double-booking rate for popular equipment categories during peak wedding seasons.  
* Peak Load Scalability: The system must handle high user concurrency without performance degradation during peak seasons when multiple Managers enter proxy records on the Web Dashboard while dozens of field teams are simultaneously syncing checklists and images.  
* Media Storage Optimization: The system must enforce automatic client-side compression routines during image evidence collection to prevent high volumes of field media files from choking cloud server storage pipelines and breaking page load speeds.

#### **4.2.3 Security:**

* Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Access control layers restrict application features strictly by role boundaries. Users (Admin, Manager, Leader, and Technical Staff) are restricted to their authorized platform web/mobile modules and cannot perform actions or view data layers outside their assigned jobs.  
* Privilege Escalation Barriers: The system architecture must block any unauthorized attempts by standard accounts to manipulate API requests or self-modify granular access settings.  
* Financial Data Encryption: Network transmissions involving financial parameters (such as customer deposit evidence, final settlements, and supplier debt records) or personally identifiable information (PII) require full 256-bit encryption protocols.  
* Credential Integrity: Account portals are guarded by strict credential policies, supporting secure internal password updates and multi-stage verification workflows whenever a user requests an automated password reset.

#### **4.2.4 Reliability & Availability:**

* Data-Driven Inventory Precision: Because real-time inventory locking relies heavily on correct user updates, the system must maintain continuous availability and prompt staff to log warehouse check-ins and check-outs immediately.  
* Absolute Report Veracity: All auto-generated reports summarizing order volumes, payment histories, outsourced Supplier debts, and session-based Staff wages must achieve 100% mathematical accuracy, fully mirroring confirmed operational data fields without any system rounding errors or data discrepancies.

## **5\. Requirement Appendix** {#5.-requirement-appendix}

### **5.1 Business Rules** {#5.1-business-rules}

| ID | Rule Definition |
| :---: | ----- |
| BR-001 | Only registered and active internal users are allowed to log into the system. |
| BR-002 | Username and password must match the stored account credentials before access is granted. |
| BR-003 | Users can access only the functions permitted by their assigned role. |
| BR-004 | Role and platform permission must be checked after authentication. |
| BR-005 | After a configurable number of consecutive failed login attempts, the account is temporarily locked according to the security policy. |
| BR-006 | Locked, inactive, or deactivated accounts cannot log into the system. |
| BR-007 | The system must invalidate the current user session and active authentication tokens after successful logout. |
| BR-008 | After logout, the user must re-authenticate before accessing protected resources or system functions. |
| BR-009 | Password recovery requires user identity verification according to the configured account recovery process. |
| BR-010 | Changing password requires the authenticated user to provide the current password and a valid new password. |
| BR-011 | New passwords must satisfy the configured password complexity and length policy. |
| BR-012 | Successful and failed authentication activities must be recorded for audit purposes. |
| BR-013 | Each internal user account must be assigned exactly one active role unless the system is explicitly configured for multiple roles. |
| BR-014 | Only Admin can create, update, deactivate, reset password, and assign role for internal user accounts. |
| BR-015 | Admin cannot deactivate their own account. |
| BR-016 | Deactivated users cannot log in, but historical business records linked to those users must be preserved. |
| BR-017 | Usernames must be unique in the system. |
| BR-018 | Inactive roles cannot be assigned to users. |
| BR-019 | Resetting a user password must be recorded in the activity log. |
| BR-020 | Admin manages equipment catalog information and preserves historical records when equipment is deactivated. |
| BR-021 | Inactive or deactivated equipment cannot be newly selected for quotation, order planning, or pick list generation. |
| BR-022 | Equipment information required for operation, inventory tracking, and compensation calculation must be completed before activation. |
| BR-023 | Equipment purchase price must be available when the equipment can be used for damage or loss compensation calculation. |
| BR-024 | Equipment catalog updates must not change historical order, quotation, checkout, or return records. |
| BR-025 | Admin can view warehouse information, but warehouse changes are limited because the business operates with a single warehouse scope. |
| BR-026 | Business policies must be configured by Admin and kept for historical reference when changed or deactivated. |
| BR-027 | Only one active policy version of the same policy type should be applied at a time. |
| BR-028 | Policy changes must not retroactively change completed orders unless explicitly adjusted by authorized users. |
| BR-029 | Deposit, cancellation, compensation, additional fee, and staff wage policies must have clear effective dates or active status. |
| BR-030 | Admin reports are view-only and must not directly modify operational data. |
| BR-031 | Customer is not a system user and does not log into the system. |
| BR-032 | Manager is responsible for registering and updating customer information used for orders and quotations. |
| BR-033 | Customer contact information should be sufficient for communication outside the system. |
| BR-034 | A quotation must be linked to customer information before it can be confirmed. |
| BR-035 | Only Manager can create, view, update, delete draft quotations, and confirm quotations. |
| BR-036 | A quotation can be deleted only if it is still in draft state and is not linked to a confirmed order. |
| BR-037 | Only active equipment, services, packages, and valid pricing can be used in a quotation. |
| BR-038 | Confirmed quotation information should be locked or versioned to preserve the agreed quotation history. |
| BR-039 | Order creation requires customer information, event date, event location, and required service/order information. |
| BR-040 | Only Manager can create, update, confirm, cancel, change event date, and close orders. |
| BR-041 | Order confirmation requires an agreed quotation and a valid confirmed deposit payment. |
| BR-042 | After order confirmation, required internal inventory must be reserved by event date. |
| BR-043 | Reserved internal inventory cannot be assigned to another confirmed order on the same event date. |
| BR-044 | Changing an event date must follow the date-change policy and requires rechecking inventory availability for the new event date. |
| BR-045 | When an order event date is changed successfully, the previous inventory reservation must be released and the new reservation must be created if inventory is available. |
| BR-046 | Order cancellation must follow the active cancellation and refund policy. |
| BR-047 | When an order is canceled, reserved inventory must be released if applicable. |
| BR-048 | An order can be closed only after required payment, settlement, handover, inventory return, supplier return/debt, damage/loss, and staff work/wage data are reviewed. |
| BR-049 | The system must preserve order status history for tracking and audit purposes. |
| BR-050 | Schedule plans are created and maintained by Manager for survey, preparation, transportation, execution, collection, and return activities. |
| BR-051 | A schedule plan cannot be deleted if it already affects confirmed assignments or active tasks. |
| BR-052 | Work tasks must be linked to an order, schedule plan, assigned staff, location, and execution requirement when applicable. |
| BR-053 | Assigned staff can view only their assigned tasks and related task details. |
| BR-054 | Work tasks that have started or have recorded attendance should not be deleted; they should be canceled or updated according to policy. |
| BR-055 | Manager can monitor survey progress and view survey reports submitted by Leader Staff. |
| BR-056 | Inventory availability must be checked or rechecked by event date. |
| BR-057 | Initial inventory checking does not reserve inventory. |
| BR-058 | Inventory availability results support quotation, supplier planning, and order confirmation decisions. |
| BR-059 | Pick lists must be generated from approved or planned order items and include item, quantity, usage, and related task information. |
| BR-060 | Manager can confirm inventory check-out only after Leader Staff submits check-out information. |
| BR-061 | Inventory return confirmation must compare checkout, collection, return, and damage/loss information. |
| BR-062 | Returned inventory quantity cannot exceed checked-out quantity unless a correction is recorded. |
| BR-063 | Damaged or lost returned equipment requires notes and evidence. |
| BR-064 | Supplier information is managed by Manager and used for rental, purchase, debt, and payment workflows. |
| BR-065 | A supplier can be deactivated for future transactions while historical supplier transactions must be preserved. |
| BR-066 | Supplier rental or purchase orders are created when internal inventory is insufficient or additional materials/equipment are required. |
| BR-067 | A supplier rental/purchase order may be saved as draft before being confirmed. |
| BR-068 | A supplier rental/purchase order can be deleted only if it has not been confirmed, received, paid, or linked to supplier debt records. |
| BR-069 | Supplier rental/purchase order updates are allowed only before the order is confirmed, received, or linked to supplier debt/payment records. |
| BR-070 | Supplier receipt information submitted by Leader Staff must include received items, quantity, condition, notes, and evidence if required. |
| BR-071 | Supplier return information must include returned quantity and condition, and must record compensation information when supplier equipment is damaged or missing. |
| BR-072 | Manager must confirm supplier receipt and return reports before they are used for supplier debt and payment review. |
| BR-073 | Supplier debt must be calculated from confirmed supplier rental/purchase, return, compensation, and payment records. |
| BR-074 | Supplier payment records must reference the related supplier transaction or debt record. |
| BR-075 | Staff wage verification must use assignments, attendance, completed tasks, wage rules, rates, deductions, and Leader Staff confirmation when applicable. |
| BR-076 | Only Manager can confirm final staff work and wage data for wage reporting. |
| BR-077 | Field operation progress must reflect preparation, transportation, setup, collection, warehouse return, and arising issues. |
| BR-078 | Change requests submitted by Leader Staff must be approved or rejected by Manager before affecting order, settlement, or inventory records. |
| BR-079 | Handover evidence submitted by Leader Staff must be reviewed and confirmed by Manager. |
| BR-080 | Damage/loss reports must include damaged or lost items, quantity, description, and evidence. |
| BR-081 | Only Manager can confirm damage/loss reports for settlement and compensation purposes. |
| BR-082 | Deposit payment request can be created only after the Customer has agreed with the quotation outside the system. |
| BR-083 | Customer payment methods include cash, manual bank transfer, and VNPay QR payment when integration is available. |
| BR-084 | VNPay QR payment status may be automatically updated based on the response from VNPay Gateway. |
| BR-085 | Cash payment must have uploaded evidence before payment confirmation. |
| BR-086 | Manual bank transfer must have uploaded transaction evidence unless valid transaction data is automatically recorded by the system. |
| BR-087 | Deposit payment must be confirmed before Manager can confirm the order. |
| BR-088 | Settlement must include original order value, change request adjustments, additional fees, compensation, deposit paid, previous payments, and remaining amount. |
| BR-089 | Customer compensation for damaged or lost equipment is calculated based on equipment purchase price and damaged/lost quantity. |
| BR-090 | Compensation amount equals equipment purchase price multiplied by damaged or lost quantity. |
| BR-091 | Final amount due equals adjusted order value plus additional fees plus compensation amount minus total paid amount. |
| BR-092 | Final payment can be confirmed only after settlement has been confirmed by Manager. |
| BR-093 | Leader Staff can upload on-site customer payment evidence, but Manager is responsible for payment confirmation. |
| BR-094 | Leader Staff can record on-site settlement information, but Manager is responsible for confirming settlement and final payment. |
| BR-095 | Staff can view only assigned tasks, task details, and pick lists related to their assigned responsibilities. |
| BR-096 | Only assigned Leader Staff can record survey reports, warehouse check-out reports, supplier receipt/return reports, field progress, change requests, damage/loss, equipment collection, inventory return, and settlement information. |
| BR-097 | Handover evidence should be uploaded when setup or handover activity is completed. |
| BR-098 | Equipment collection records must be completed after the event and before warehouse return verification. |
| BR-099 | Inventory return reports submitted by Leader Staff must be available for Manager verification. |
| BR-100 | Staff attendance must be linked to assigned work sessions. |
| BR-101 | Leader Staff confirmation of Technical Staff attendance and work completion is required as supporting data for Manager wage verification. |
| BR-102 | Technical Staff cannot confirm their own work completion for wage calculation purposes. |
| BR-103 | All evidence files for payment, handover, damage/loss, supplier receipt/return, and settlement must be stored with the related business record. |
| BR-104 | Users must receive notifications only for information related to their role, responsibilities, assignments, approvals, or operational events. |
| BR-105 | All create, update, deactivate, confirm, cancel, payment, and approval actions must be recorded in the activity log. |
| BR-106 | System-generated reports must reflect the latest confirmed operational data and preserve historical records for audit. |
| BR-107 | Draft records can be edited or deleted only when they have not affected confirmed operational, payment, supplier, inventory, or wage records. |
| BR-108 | Confirmed records should be changed only through authorized update, cancellation, or adjustment workflows rather than direct deletion. |
